units.source_statement: Continuation from previous page says second lord in exaltation gives great hope of recovery, particularly with additional good recovery testimony.
preconditions: Second lord in its exaltation AND any stated extra support.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Do not replace a conditional hope with certainty.

units.source_statement: A new source heading Of Theft introduces a separate list of alleged property-recovery and thief-related rules.
preconditions: Begins after the prior exaltation sentence.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Textual heading is original; nearby handwritten numbering is not a printed chapter number.

units.source_statement: Seventh lord in ascendant is claimed to mean the theft/goods shall be restored.
preconditions: Lord7 in first.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This is in the Of Theft subsection, not the later in-person capture inquiry.

units.source_statement: Ascendant lord in seventh is said to mean the lost goods will be found only after much inquiry.
preconditions: Lord1 in seventh.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Timing qualifier 'after much enquiry' essential.

units.source_statement: Moon in ascendant OR Moon with the ascendant lord is said to mean the stolen goods may be found.
preconditions: Moon in first or joined to lord1.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The original hedges 'shall or may'; not categorical.

units.source_statement: Moon in first WITH the ascendant lord is a more specific recovery claim.
preconditions: Both Moon and first lord occupy first.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: May overlap the previous source alternatives, not an independent person/case.

units.source_statement: Sun and Moon in first, together with eighth lord and first lord in first, form a stronger source configuration predicting goods found.
preconditions: The printed clause may conjoin Sun/Moon in first and lord8 with lord1 in first.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Nested source syntax unclear; retain rather than imposing one exact Boolean structure.

units.source_statement: Second lord in eighth again means the goods cannot be had.
preconditions: Lord2 occupies house8.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Repetition from earlier negative recovery passage.

units.source_statement: Saturn, Mars or Dragon Tail in second are said to mean the property will not be recovered.
preconditions: One named negative body in house2.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Do not infer any real theft.

units.source_statement: Lord2 in ascendant means the goods are recovered, but no one knows how.
preconditions: Lord2 in first.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Keep 'none shall know how' source claim.

units.source_statement: First lord in second is said to give recovery after great labour.
preconditions: Lord1 in house2.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Separately qualified delay/difficulty.

units.source_statement: Second lord cadent from an angle is said to deny recovery.
preconditions: Lord2 cadent.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The text juxtaposes a positive exaltation exception.

units.source_statement: Second lord in exaltation is said to make quick restoration, especially when Moon applies to that lord.
preconditions: Lord2 exalted; applying Moon strengthens time claim.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Different from a generic exalted planet.

units.source_statement: A heading Other Judgments of Thefts begins another set of source-tested rules.
preconditions: Original separate subsection after Of Theft.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Do not pool multiple similar rules as independent observed outcomes.

units.source_statement: First lord and seventh lord joined are said to mean the stolen good/thief is found through the querent's searching.
preconditions: Applying joining of the two relevant lords.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Lilly's subject is the thing sought under a theft question, not validated identification.

units.source_statement: First lord in seventh OR joined to lord8 OR seventh lord in ascendant are claimed to mean the thief returns of his own accord before going farther.
preconditions: One of three printed alternative configurations.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Lilly says he observed this often, but no independently authenticated cohort is provided.

units.source_statement: Moon separating from first lord and joining seventh lord is interpreted as the thief being found.
preconditions: Order: past separation from first THEN joining seventh.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Do not reverse with Moon separating seventh then joining first, which appears elsewhere.

units.source_statement: Seventh lord joined to an infortune IN AN ANGLE is said to mean the alleged thief will be taken.
preconditions: Lord7 conjunct infortune and angular.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Distinct from 'not taken' Fortune branch.

units.source_statement: Seventh lord joined to a Fortune is said not to be taken unless that Fortune is under Sun's beams or otherwise impeded.
preconditions: Lord7 with benefic and source exception (under beams/impeded).
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Do not claim a natural fortune absolutely prevents capture.

units.source_statement: If thief's seventh-house ruler goes toward combustion, source claims his death.
preconditions: Seventh lord applying to combustion.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Historical mortality claim is not modern forensic or medical evidence.

units.source_statement: Moon joined to an unfortunate planet is said to mean the thief will be found.
preconditions: Moon joined to infortune under source context.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Not proof any specific person is a thief.

units.source_statement: Moon joined to retrograde planet is said to mean alleged thief returns of his own accord.
preconditions: Moon joined to retrograde body.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The author claims he found this true, but does not provide blinded case records.

units.source_statement: Continuation states that if that planet is stationary, the thief does not move from his place until taken.
preconditions: The planet of the preceding Moon-to-retrograde comparison is stationary.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Distinguish stationary body from retrograde body and from geographical distance.

units.source_statement: A new heading Whether the Thief shall be knowne or not opens recognition rules.
preconditions: Scope is knowing/not knowing the alleged offender.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Do not use this to identify any real person.

units.source_statement: Lilly says the majority of planets occupying cadent houses indicates alleged thief will be known.
preconditions: MOST planets cadent, not one cadent planet.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Source makes strong inference with no evidence of detection.

units.source_statement: Sun in conjunction, square or opposition to the thief significator is claimed to make the thief known.
preconditions: Sun (☉) in conjunction (☌), square (□), or opposition (☍) to thief significator; the original p360 line4 has a same-volume errata entry.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Conjunction omitted from producer paraphrase; restored from original PDF394 line and p360/l4 errata. Exact editorial role of erratum remains uncertain; no claim of real thief identification.

units.source_statement: Sun sextile the thief's significator is said to make him suspected but not openly known.
preconditions: Source Sun-to-thief sextile as distinct from square/opposition.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: No factual basis for suspecting people.

units.source_statement: A distinct heading Whether the Thief be suspected of the Owner or not introduces suspicion mechanics.
preconditions: Owner/suspect distinction.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Predictions about suspicion are not criminal truth.

units.source_statement: Thief significator square/opposition to first lord yields owner suspicion, whereas trine/sextile to first lord is said not to.
preconditions: Compare thief significator vs ascendant lord; aspect polarity.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: No independent measure of actual suspicion.

units.source_statement: Thief significator in conjunction with Moon is said to mean owner suspects a person in company with himself or using his company.
preconditions: Relevant thief significator bodily joined to Moon.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The statement concerns owner's belief, not culprit identity.

units.source_statement: Moon square/opposed to a planet in tenth or seventh is said to make owner suspect someone distant, unless the relevant house almuten aspects the Moon adversely.
preconditions: Moon hard aspect to planet in named house, plus exception.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: House-almuten exception and 'far' subject uncertain; preserve.

units.source_statement: Moon conjunct/square/opposed to a planet in seventh or its almuten is said to cause suspicion of that house's person.
preconditions: Moon's adverse aspect to occupant or almuten of seventh.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This is owner's suspicion, not proof.

units.source_statement: If Moon instead aspects another planet, the owner is said to suspect that different person rather than the thief.
preconditions: Moon's actual aspect is to OTHER planet.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Useful negative distinction: suspected person may differ from culprit.

units.source_statement: If Moon is joined to or received by an evil planet, source identifies the suspected one with the alleged thief.
preconditions: Moon joined/received by an ill planet in author's interpretation.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Do not claim a particular person guilty based on Moon.

units.source_statement: Lilly asks reader to compare strength of first lord and Moon and any virtue received/separated from evil planets to decide who acted.
preconditions: Specific earlier ill-planet transfers to first or Moon.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The grammar and temporal direction are complex; retain source uncertainty.

units.source_statement: Ascendant lord angular applying or separating to a planet in cadent house is said to tell truth about the theft.
preconditions: First lord angular, and aspecting cadent planet.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The source uses 'truth is said of him'; not independent verification of honest testimony.

units.source_statement: Moon joined to an angular planet, especially in tenth, is offered as parallel truthfulness testimony.
preconditions: Moon actually conjunct planet angular.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Do not substitute ordinary Moon aspect to any tenth planet.

units.source_statement: A new heading Who did the Deed or Theft begins offender-classification by houses and luminary placements.
preconditions: Historical speculative attribution.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Must not be used for real accusation or identity inference.

units.source_statement: Ascendant lord in the second, sixth or seventh, OR second lord in ascendant, is claimed to implicate the owner himself in the source's offender-classification list.
preconditions: Original printed 'second, sixt or seventh': sixt denotes sixth house, NOT first house.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The producer draft misread printed 'sixt' as 'first'. This historical criminal accusation rule is not valid forensic evidence.

units.source_statement: Sun and Moon in fourth are assigned alleged deed to father, mother or friend.
preconditions: Luminaries in fourth.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Multiple alleged relation roles; no actual named culprit.

units.source_statement: Sun or Moon in fifth is associated with son or daughter of owner.
preconditions: Either Sun or Moon in fifth.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Do not combine fifth-lord mediation from other chapter.

units.source_statement: Sun or Moon in first is associated in this list with a servant.
preconditions: Either Sun or Moon in ascendant.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This conflicts with another own-house condition implicating owner; keep chart context.

units.source_statement: Sun or Moon in seventh is assigned a wife in the source relationship-classification list.
preconditions: Luminary in seventh.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Page395 continues with Sun-Moon mutual aspects and domestic acquaintance variants.

units.source_statement: Sun and Moon conjoined and beholding ascendant are linked to an acquaintance of owner; source also gives either luminary beholding ascendant as similar.
preconditions: Together plus first-house aspect, or alternative single aspect.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This is a generic classification, not independently verified acquaintance.

units.source_statement: Sun or Moon in its proper house or in ascendant is said to make owner himself justly suspected.
preconditions: At least one luminary in own house or first under source's later variant.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This contradicts some other source relationship categories and is not proof.

units.source_statement: If Sun and Moon are not together but one beholds ascendant, source suggests someone once born or previously resident in the house.
preconditions: The lights are separated, one beholding first.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Do not conflate an acquaintance with a former resident or newborn.

units.source_statement: Sun or Moon in their own triplicity are said to indicate a thief familiar with the person who lost the goods.
preconditions: Luminary in own triplicity.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The author distinguishes this from a member of the owner's family.

units.source_statement: Sun or Moon having only a face dignity is said to identify a kinsman, not a household member.
preconditions: Only face rather than triplicity as key dignity.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Historical social-role inference not verified.

units.source_statement: Sun or Moon beholding ascendant but not the thief significator is said to mean alleged thief did not enter the house before taking.
preconditions: Moon/Sun aspect to first and nonaspect to thief significator.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Speculative reconstruction of an act.

units.source_statement: Thief's significator holding great essential dignities in ascendant is said to indicate kin or close acquaintance of querent.
preconditions: Thief significator dignified in first.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Not evidence of familial involvement.

units.source_statement: Mars as thief significator in tenth is said to implicate querent himself or great negligence.
preconditions: Mars must represent thief and be in tenth.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Author offers two disjunct explanations; no verified negligence.

units.source_statement: Seventh lord in ascendant makes owner suspect the thief in source's allegation.
preconditions: Lord7 physically first.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Concerns suspicion rather than prosecution or proof.

units.source_statement: A new heading asks Whether it be the first fact the Thief hath committed.
preconditions: Scope is purported previous offences.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: No external criminal record or repeat-offender rate.

units.source_statement: Sun and Moon both beholding the lord of Moon's house from an angle is said to mean the suspected thief acted more than once.
preconditions: Both luminaries and specific lord/angular condition.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: A historical prediction of past crime, not evidence of recidivism.

units.source_statement: The Part of Fortune (⊗) OR seventh-house lord free from misfortunes, OR Jupiter alone as thief significator, is said by Lilly to signify the alleged person's first offence.
preconditions: Original PDF395/printed361 prints the Part-of-Fortune glyph (circle and diagonal cross), not the indefinite word 'Fortune'. The three branches are alternatives.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Historical offender-description claim with no independently verified accuracy; do not interpret the symbol as a generic benefic planet.

units.source_statement: Mars separating from seventh lord is assigned to more than first offence.
preconditions: Mars separation from house7 lord.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Do not transpose separation direction.

units.source_statement: Saturn oriental is assigned to a previous offence in the same source list.
preconditions: Saturn in oriental condition.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: No established age/time or observed crime.

units.source_statement: Mars as thief significator is said to indicate breaking in by violence.
preconditions: Mars assigned as thief in this paragraph.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Cannot infer actual forced entry.

units.source_statement: Venus in the thief-offence paragraph is associated with action under a pretext of love.
preconditions: Venus identified with relevant thief significator.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Gendered interpretation, not motive evidence.

units.source_statement: Mercury is associated with subtlety, flattery or deception in the same historical classification.
preconditions: Mercury relevant to thief's role.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: No verified fraud or psychological trait.

units.source_statement: A new heading Of Theft by Astrologie, or LILLIES best experienced Rules introduces another authorial method set.
preconditions: Original subheading near lower PDF395.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Lilly's claim of experience is not independently evaluated.

units.source_statement: Many peregrine planets in angles are said to indicate multiple thieves.
preconditions: Peregrine status AND angular placement of multiple planets.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This is source count doctrine, not a measured number of offenders.

units.source_statement: Thief significator in fruitful or bicorporeal signs, or beholding many peregrines, is also said to imply many thieves.
preconditions: Specific source sign category or aspect to many peregrines.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Original bicorporeal printed sign list is subject to glyph/source collation.

units.source_statement: Fixed angles or Moon/thief significator in certain direct ascension/unfruitful signs is said to imply one thief.
preconditions: Fixed angles OR named Moon/significator sign groups.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The listed sign sets overlap source categories; do not silently normalize.
